name: Salesforce
description: Enterprise CRM and platform for sales, service, marketing, and custom app development.
gating_notes: Free Developer Edition org signup at developer.salesforce.com gives full API access (capped at 15,000 requests/day); production access typically comes with a paid org but developer/trial orgs are free and unrestricted for building.
mcp_notes: Official Salesforce MCP server exists (60+ tools) alongside REST/SOAP/Bulk/GraphQL(pilot) APIs.

name: HubSpot
description: CRM and marketing/sales/service platform with a broad suite of inbound marketing and pipeline tools.
gating_notes: Private apps (instant access token) are available on most plans including the free tier; OAuth apps require a HubSpot developer account, which is free to create.
mcp_notes: Official HubSpot MCP server (public beta), developers.hubspot.com/ai-tools/mcp, plus a separate developer-platform MCP.

name: Pipedrive
description: Sales-pipeline-focused CRM for small and mid-size sales teams.
gating_notes: API token can be grabbed directly from any Pipedrive account (trial included); a developer sandbox account is also available on request for building OAuth apps.
mcp_notes: Pipedrive released an official MCP server (reported June 2026), available on every plan.

name: Attio
description: Modern, flexible/customizable CRM built around a relational data model.
gating_notes: API key can be self-generated from workspace developer settings; Attio offers a free trial of paid plans, so a developer can get API access without a sales conversation, though exact free-tier API limits weren't confirmed in docs.
mcp_notes: Attio MCP integration exists with 40+ tools (lists, meetings, calls/transcripts) per third-party roundups; unclear if official or community-maintained.

name: Twenty
description: Open-source CRM alternative to Salesforce, self-hostable or used via Twenty's cloud.
gating_notes: Fully open source (self-hostable) and API keys are generated directly from Settings > API & Webhooks with no approval process; cloud version also allows self-serve signup.
mcp_notes: No single official MCP server confirmed, but multiple actively maintained community MCP servers exist (e.g. mhenry3164/twenty-crm-mcp-server, IgorWarzocha/twenty-mcp-server); an official one was requested via GitHub issue #12953.

name: Podio
description: Customizable work/project-management and CRM platform (now operated by Progress Software).
gating_notes: Developer docs describe grabbing an API key per app from account settings after agreeing to terms of use; no paid-plan gate mentioned, though the product's ongoing investment level is uncertain after being spun out to Progress Software in 2025.
mcp_notes: No official or notable community MCP server found for Podio.

name: Zoho CRM
description: CRM component of the broader Zoho SaaS suite, covering sales pipeline, automation, and analytics.
gating_notes: Any Zoho account (including the free plan, up to 3 users / 5,000 API credits per day) can access the API console and generate OAuth clients; a free Developer Edition is also offered for testing — no sales/approval gate.
mcp_notes: No production-ready official MCP server found as of research; only informal/community efforts noted despite Zoho's large install base.

name: Close
description: Sales CRM built for inside-sales teams with built-in calling, SMS, and email.
gating_notes: API keys are generated directly by any Close user/trial account from settings; Close offers a free trial, so developers can self-serve without a sales conversation.
mcp_notes: Close has a calling-CRM MCP server with a three-tier scope model (read / write_safe / write_destructive) per third-party coverage; official status not fully confirmed but appears first-party.

name: Copper
description: CRM built tightly around Google Workspace/Gmail for relationship-driven sales teams.
gating_notes: Copper offers a free trial signup, and API keys can be generated by admin users from System Settings; full API access effectively requires an active (trial or paid) Copper account and admin role.
mcp_notes: No official or notable community MCP server found for Copper.

name: DealCloud
description: Enterprise deal/relationship-management platform (by Intapp) built for private equity, investment banking, and M&A firms.
gating_notes: DealCloud is sold enterprise-only to existing client sites; API access requires an existing DealCloud site plus a site Admin to enable the 'API' capability for a user group and issue keys — no public self-serve developer signup or free trial found.
mcp_notes: No official or community MCP server found for DealCloud.
blocker: Requires an existing paid DealCloud client site and admin-provisioned access; no public free trial or self-serve developer sandbox, so Composio could build the toolkit but end users need an existing enterprise contract to use it.
